memory_update.text: APPN added as underfollowed AI workflow/governance candidate; key survival test is whether AI features materially improve subscription growth, retention, regulated-industry wins, and cash conversion.
PATH added as underfollowed agentic automation/orchestration candidate; key survival test is ARR acceleration, net retention, production AI-agent deployments, and margin discipline.

DT added as observability/AIOps and telemetry-governance candidate; key survival test is whether AI observability and telemetry governance create incremental ARR rather than simply rebranding standard monitoring.

DOMO added as speculative small-cap data-readiness candidate; key survival test is whether consumption ARR, net retention, and AI data-product adoption improve despite flat revenue and strategic-alternatives uncertainty.
For AI software, the likely chokepoint is not model access alone but the governed conversion of enterprise data into auditable, secure, production workflows.

Cloud revenue quality should remain a separate falsification workstream; future layers should check whether reported AI/cloud growth is arm's-length demand or partly influenced by vendor investments, credits, or commercial entanglements.

node: AI software, automation, data platforms, and cloud revenue quality
summary: Expanded the AI software/data-workflow node with a two-lane universe focused on enterprise AI deployment chokepoints rather than generic model access. The strongest underfollowed lane candidates are workflow/process automation, observability/telemetry governance, and operational data platforms where AI adoption depends on data readiness, auditability, regulated workflows, and measurable automation ROI. Revenue-quality risk remains a separate falsification track: cloud/AI revenue may need scrutiny for commercial entanglements, customer-funded credits, or non-arm's-length demand.
